subject: Field prep: on‑prem K8s cluster topology and hardware affinity — preflight items
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Diego Alvarez <diego@acmetech.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Field prep: on‑prem K8s cluster topology and hardware affinity — preflight items

Diego / Acme ops team,

Thanks again for agreeing to host Redwood in your datacenter next month. Before the preflight call, I wanted to capture the minimal inputs we'll need to produce a final BOM and node-pool layout. This will help us avoid rework on the call and speed up procurement. Attached is a short questionnaire (initial_capacity_questions.pdf) — below are the key items we usually need from customers running our private deployment. If you can paste answers into a reply or attach the rack/network PDF that would be ideal.

High-level asks (short answers OK):
- Primary availability model: single-site with N+1 racks or multi-site?
- Physical constraints: number of racks, per-rack switches, cross-rack uplink speed (Gbps).
- Hypervisor/Provisioning: vSphere (versions), metal PXE, or HCI?
- Expected steady-state workload: number of steady pods, peak burst pods, % GPU workload.
- GPU details: model, perf targets (fp16/amp), driver constraints.
- Storage platform: Ceph/NetApp/Isilon/local SSD — desired PV types, replication factor, expected IOPS/TB.
- Network: separate management/control plane VLANs, storage VLANs, public egress/egress NAT expectations.
- RTO/RPO and retention windows for LLM KV cache and user data.
- Compliance evidence needs (SOC2, encryption-at-rest, KMS).

Prelim proposal (we'll refine):
- Control plane: 3 control nodes (non-tenant), anti-affinity across racks.
- Worker pools: compute-gpu (2 nodes to start), compute-cpu (6-8), infra (logging/monitoring, 3 small nodes), storage nodes sized for Ceph if using.
- Storage: recommend mixing local NVMe for Redis/KV caches (low latency) and Ceph for persistent model artifacts.
- Networking: dual-homed NICs for storage/tenant traffic separation; BGP or static routes for cluster egress; egress NAT at edge.

Next step: send the answers and your dc_rack_layout (if available). I'll assemble a draft BOM and a preflight checklist and share it back. Can we hold a 60-minute preflight on Tuesday 2028-07-18? Marcus / Mina / Lauren will be on the call.

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Re: Field prep: on‑prem K8s cluster topology and hardware affinity — preflight items

Marcus — thanks for the checklist. Answers below and I've attached our rack diagram (dc_rack_layout.pdf).

- Primary availability: single-site (two racks dedicated to compute). We do not have multi-site replication planned.
- Physical constraints: 2 compute racks + 1 services rack. Top-of-rack switches are 40Gb, cross-rack spine is 10Gb between those racks (we realize this is a bottleneck).
- Provisioning: vSphere 7.0u3 for most nodes; we can provide dedicated VMs or bare-metal, preference is bare-metal for GPU hosts.
- Steady-state workload: ~120 steady pods, peaks up to ~300 during batch jobs. Approx 20% of pods will require GPUs at peak.
- GPUs: 2 x A40 per GPU host (we have two hosts budgeted initially). Drivers: NVIDIA 525 driver in our environment.
- Storage: Ceph backend managed by our infra team, currently configured with 3 OSDs per storage node. Target for model artifacts: 200TB replicated with RF=3, IOPS requirement for KV cache ~50k read/s.
- Network: we already have management VLAN and a separate storage VLAN. Public egress is through a NAT gateway in the services rack.
- RTO/RPO: KV cache can be rebuilt from model artifacts within 2 hours (RTO). User data retention 30 days.
- Compliance: SOC2 in-scope; we will need documentation for encryption-at-rest and audit logs.

Notes: we can provide hardware BOM draft and SNs for bare-metal if helpful. Happy to go over this on Tue 18th.

—Diego

Subject: Re: Field prep: on‑prem K8s cluster topology and hardware affinity — preflight items

Diego — appreciate the detail and the rack diagram, that helps a lot. Below I sketched a concrete starting configuration and flagged open items. I'm attaching a preflight checklist (redwood_onprem_preflight_checklist.xlsx) and a draft hardware BOM (hardware_bom_draft.csv).

Summary recommendation (startup configuration):
- Control plane: 3 controller VMs/bare-metal in the services rack. Use static CIDRs and dedicated control VLAN. Ensure supervisors are spread across both physical switches to tolerate a switch failure.
- Node pools:
  * compute-gpu: 2 bare-metal nodes, each with 2 x A40, local NVMe + 2x10Gb NICs (one for tenant traffic, one for storage). Reserve 10% headroom for driver/kernel updates.
  * compute-cpu: 6 bare-metal nodes, 256GB RAM, 24 vCPU equivalent; provision as a single node-pool with podAntiAffinity for stateful services. autoscaler: min 4 / max 12.
  * infra: 3 small nodes (loki/tempo/prometheus/elasticsearch, ingress), 64GB RAM.
  * storage: 3 Ceph OSD hosts (or use existing Ceph cluster if you prefer) sized for 200TB usable with RF=3. We recommend 10Gb links between OSDs; if cross-rack 10Gb is the limiting factor, we will size IO-intensive workloads to local NVMe when possible.

Storage guidance:
- Use local NVMe for LLM KV caches (low-latency). KV cache should be configured as ephemeral PVCs and backed up nightly to Ceph for rebuildability.
- Put model artifacts on Ceph RBD with thin provisioning; use placement groups tuned for 200TB and RF=3.
- For large batch reads, enable read-ahead on the Ceph client side and prefer block storage access paths.

Network and affinity:
- Two-NIC topology: separate management/storage and tenant traffic. Enforce egress NAT at the services rack with iptables/edge NAT.
- Node affinity: pin GPU pods to compute-gpu pool via nodeSelector + tolerations for GPU runtime. Use topologySpreadConstraints to distribute GPUs across hosts.
- Cross-rack bandwidth limit: because spine is 10Gb, schedule IO-heavy pods to avoid cross-rack chatter; we can use a kube-scheduler extender or node taints to preferentially co-locate workloads.

Compliance and ops:
- We'll need SOC2 artifacts: encryption-at-rest config for Ceph, KMS integration details, and audit log retention policy. Mina will lead the SOC2 evidence collection.

Open items (please confirm):
1) Can you confirm whether the Ceph cluster will be dedicated to Redwood workloads or shared?
2) Do you want local NVMe for model artifacts or only for KV cache?
3) Can infra team provide a VLAN map for storage and management VLANs?

Scheduling: Tue 2028-07-18 10:00 PT works for our team — I've tentatively booked 60 minutes. If that time is bad for you, propose an alternative.

Thanks,
Marcus

Attachments: redwood_onprem_preflight_checklist.xlsx, hardware_bom_draft.csv
